Example Shloka: धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः। मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय॥
Transliteration: dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ | māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya ||
Translation/Source: “In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra, assembled and eager to fight, what did my sons and the Pandavas do, O Sanjaya?” – Bhagavad Gita 1.1

Example Shloka: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि। धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्॥
Transliteration: tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ||
Translation/Source: The famous Gayatri Mantra – Rigveda 3.62.10

Example Shloka: इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान्। एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदन्ति॥
Transliteration: indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṃ sad viprā bahudhā vadanti ||
Translation/Source: “They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni, and the divine Suparna Garuda. The one reality, the wise call by many names.” – Rigveda 1.164.46

Example Shloka: यस्य छाया अमृतं यस्य मृत्युर्यस्य ब्रह्म परमं च धाम। को वेद तत्त्वमृषिर्यो ददर्श॥
Transliteration: yasya chāyā amṛtaṃ yasya mṛtyur yasya brahma paramaṃ ca dhāma | ko veda tattvam ṛṣir yo dadarśa ||
Translation/Source: “Whose shadow is immortality, whose shadow is death, whose supreme abode is Brahman – which sage who has seen knows that reality?” – Atharvaveda

Example Shloka: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्॥
Transliteration: agne naya supathā rāye asmān ||
Translation/Source: “O Agni, lead us by the good path to prosperity” – Shukla Yajurveda

Example Shloka: पञ्चजना मम होत्रा जुषन्तां पञ्च सेधन्तु दुरितानि विश्वा॥
Transliteration: pañcajanā mama hotrā juṣantāṃ pañca sedhantu duritāni viśvā ||
Translation/Source: From Rigvedic hymns addressing the five peoples

Example Shloka: बृहद्यशो बृहतः पुत्र आसीद्बृहस्पतिर्बृहतो जायत। बृहन्नमो बृहते वीर्याय॥
Transliteration: bṛhadyaśo bṛhataḥ putra āsīd bṛhaspatirbṛhato jāyata | bṛhannamo bṛhate vīryāya ||
Translation/Source: “Great was the glory, great was the son, Brihaspati was born of the great. Great salutation to the great prowess.”

Example Shloka: षड्विधा हि समिधस्ते अग्ने॥
Transliteration: ṣaḍvidhā hi samidhaste agne ||
Translation/Source: “Six-fold indeed are your fuel-sticks, O Agni”

Example Shloka: विराड्वै पादोऽस्य सर्वा भूतानि त्रिपादस्यामृतं दिवि॥
Transliteration: virāḍvai pādo’sya sarvā bhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi ||
Translation/Source: “Viraj is indeed his foot; all beings are his three-fold immortal part in heaven” – Purusha Sukta

Example Shloka: प्रस्तरे सुप्रस्तरे आ कृण्वन्तु त्वा नरो महते सौभगाय॥
Transliteration: prastare suprastare ā kṛṇvantu tvā naro mahate saubhagāya ||
Translation/Source: From Rigvedic compositions

Example Shloka: महाबृहती छन्दसां राज्ञी सर्वा भूतानि बिभर्ति॥
Transliteration: mahābṛhatī chandasāṃ rājñī sarvā bhūtāni bibharti ||
Translation/Source: “Mahabrihati, the queen of meters, supports all beings”

Example Shloka: शक्वरी छन्दसि प्रोक्ता चतुर्दशाक्षरा मता॥
Transliteration: śakvarī chandasi proktā caturdaśākṣarā matā ||
Translation/Source: Technical description from Chandas Shastra

Example Shloka: स्वागतं ते कुशलिनो गुरो प्रीतिकरा गिरः। आशीर्वादमयी देवि सरस्वति नमोऽस्तु ते॥
Transliteration: svāgataṃ te kuśalino guro prītikara giraḥ | āśīrvādamayī devi sarasvati namo’stu te ||
Translation/Source: “Welcome, O auspicious teacher, your words bring joy. O goddess Saraswati, filled with blessings, salutations to you.” – Classical Sanskrit

Example Shloka: गुरुब्रह्मा गुरुर्विष्णुर्गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः। गुरुः साक्षात्परं ब्रह्म तस्मै श्रीगुरवे नमः॥
Transliteration: gurubrahma guruviṣṇur gururdevo maheśvaraḥ | guruḥ sākṣāt paraṃ brahma tasmai śrīgurave namaḥ ||
Translation/Source: “Guru is Brahma, Guru is Vishnu, Guru is the god Maheshwara. Guru is verily the Supreme Brahman, salutations to that revered Guru.” – Traditional

Example Shloka: सकलजगत्कारण कारुणिक करुणाकर। शरणागत वत्सल श्रीरामचन्द्र नमामि॥
Transliteration: sakalajagatkaraṇa karuṇika karuṇākara | śaraṇāgata vatsala śrīrāmacandra namāmi ||
Translation/Source: “O cause of the entire universe, compassionate ocean of mercy, loving to those who surrender, I bow to Sri Ramachandra.” – Devotional literature

Example Shloka: वन्दे गुरुपरम्परां श्रुतिसिद्धान्तसारभूताम्। ब्रह्मानन्दसरस्वतीं जगद्गुरुं शङ्करम्॥
Transliteration: vande guruparamparāṃ śrutisiddhāntasārabhūtām | brahmānandasarasvatīṃ jagadguruṃ śaṅkaram ||
Translation/Source: “I bow to the guru tradition, which is the essence of scriptural conclusions, to Brahmananda Saraswati, the world guru Shankara.” – Advaitic literature

Example Shloka: नीलकण्ठ महेशान विश्वनाथ गिरीश शम्भो। त्रिशूलपाणे डमरूधर शिव शङ्कर नमोऽस्तु ते॥
Transliteration: nīlakaṇṭha maheśāna viśvanātha girīśa śambho | triśūlapāṇe ḍamarūdhara śiva śaṅkara namo’stu te ||
Translation/Source: “O blue-necked Maheshana, Lord of the universe, mountain lord Shambhu, wielder of trident and drum, O Shiva Shankara, salutations to you.” – Shaivite hymns

Example Shloka: पञ्चचामरसंयुक्ते महारानि महेश्वरि। सर्वलोकनमस्कृते देवि त्वां शरणं गताः॥
Transliteration: pañcacāmarasaṃyukte mahārāni maheśvari | sarvalokanamaskṛte devi tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
Translation/Source: “O great queen, great goddess, adorned with five whisks, worshipped by all worlds, O goddess, we have come to your refuge.” – Devi literature

Example Shloka: शिखरिणी छन्दसि रम्या सप्तदशाक्षरसंयुता। कवीनां प्रियतमा यस्मात्तस्मात्शिखरिणी मता॥
Transliteration: śikhariṇī chandasi ramyā saptadaśākṣarasaṃyutā | kavīnāṃ priyatamā yasmāt tasmāt śikhariṇī matā ||
Translation/Source: “Shikharini meter is beautiful, having seventeen syllables. Since it is most beloved of poets, it is therefore called Shikharini.” – Prosody texts

Example Shloka: शार्दूलविक्रीडितमिदं छन्दो नवदशाक्षरम्। महाकवीनां हृदयं हरति स्वमधुरध्वनिना॥
Transliteration: śārdūlavikrīḍitamidaṃ chando navadaśākṣaram | mahākavīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ harati svamadhuradhjvaninā ||
Translation/Source: “This Shardula-vikriditam meter has nineteen syllables. It captivates the hearts of great poets with its own sweet sound.” – Classical poetry

Example Shloka: मात्राकालं समं यत्र तत्मात्रासमकं विदुः। चतुर्विंशतिमात्रा वा द्वात्रिंशन्मात्रका तथा॥
Transliteration: mātrākālaṃ samaṃ yatra tatmātrāsamakaṃ viduḥ | caturviṃśatimātrā vā dvātriṃśanmātrakā tathā ||
Translation/Source: “Where the time-units (matras) are equal, that is known as matra-samaka. It may have twenty-four matras or thirty-two matras.” – Chandas Shastra

Example Shloka: वागर्थाविव सम्प्रक्तौ वागर्थप्रतिपत्तये। जगतः पितरौ वन्दे पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ॥
Transliteration: vāgarthāviva sampraktau vāgarthapratipattaye | jagataḥ pitarau vande pārvatīparameśvarau ||
Translation/Source: “I bow to the parents of the universe, Parvati and Parameshwara, who are united like word and meaning, for the understanding of word and meaning.” – Raghuvamsha 1.1

Example Shloka: स गच्छन्गच्छतां श्रेष्ठो ययौ गौरीगुरोर्गृहम्। शैलाधिराजकन्याया मनोज्ञां दर्शनेच्छया॥
Transliteration: sa gacchan gacchatāṃ śreṣṭho yayau gaurīguror gṛham | śailādhirājakanyāyā manojñāṃ darśanecchayā ||
Translation/Source: “He, the best among those who go, went to Gauri’s teacher’s house, with the desire to see the charming daughter of the mountain king.” – Kumarasambhava

Example Shloka: वंशस्थं द्वादशाक्षरं यति चतुर्थे अष्टमे तथा। लघुगुरुमयं रम्यं कवयो येन रञ्जिताः॥
Transliteration: vaṃśasthaṃ dvādaśākṣaraṃ yati caturthe aṣṭame tathā | laghugurumayaṃ ramyaṃ kavayo yena rañjitāḥ ||
Translation/Source: “Vamshastha has twelve syllables, with caesura at the fourth and eighth. Composed of short and long syllables, it is beautiful and delights poets.” – Prosody manuals

Example Shloka: द्रुतविलम्बितं छन्दो गुरुभिर्लघुभिश्च यत्। मिश्रितं मधुरं तत्तु कविहृदयहारि च॥
Transliteration: drutavilambitaṃ chando gurubhir laghubhiś ca yat | miśritaṃ madhuraṃ tattu kavihṛdayahāri ca ||
Translation/Source: “Drutavilambita meter, which is mixed with heavy and light syllables, is sweet and captivates the hearts of poets.” – Classical texts

Example Shloka: मन्दाक्रान्ता सप्तदशाक्षरा श्रीमती गुरुलघ्वक्षरैर्युता। सा चेत्कान्ता काव्यरसास्वादे हरति चित्तं कविकुलस्य नः॥
Transliteration: mandākrāntā saptadaśākṣarā śrīmatī gurulagh-vakṣaira yutā | sā cet kāntā kāvyarasāsvāde harati cittaṃ kavikulasya naḥ ||
Translation/Source: “Mandakranta, having seventeen syllables, endowed with heavy and light syllables, when beautiful in poetic sentiment, captivates the hearts of our poet community.” – Classical poetry

Example Shloka: आर्या गाथा प्राकृते बहुला संस्कृते तथा। मात्रावृत्तं तु तत्प्रोक्तमाचार्यैः छन्दशास्त्रवित्॥
Transliteration: āryā gāthā prākṛte bahulā saṃskṛte tathā | mātrāvṛttaṃ tu tat proktam ācāryaiḥ chandaśāstravit ||
Translation/Source: “Arya gatha is abundant in Prakrit and also in Sanskrit. That is called matra-vritta by the teachers who know prosody.” – Pingala’s Chandas Shastra

Example Shloka: पुष्पिताग्रं द्वादश च यतिर्द्वितीयषष्ठयोः। सप्तमे च दशमे वा सुन्दरं छन्द उच्यते॥
Transliteration: puṣpitāgraṃ dvādaśa ca yatir dvitīyaṣaṣṭhayoḥ | saptame ca daśame vā sundaraṃ chanda ucyate ||
Translation/Source: “Pushpitagra has twelve syllables, with caesura at the second and sixth, or at the seventh and tenth. It is called a beautiful meter.” – Prosody texts

Example Shloka: पृथ्वी छन्दः सप्तदशाक्षरो गुरुलघुर्मिश्रो महाकविप्रियः। भूमण्डलस्य नामेन यतो नाम समर्पितं तस्य॥
Transliteration: pṛthvī chandaḥ saptadaśākṣaro gurulghur miśro mahākavipriyaḥ | bhūmaṇḍalasya nāmena yato nāma samarpitaṃ tasya ||
Translation/Source: “Prithvi meter has seventeen syllables, mixed with heavy and light, beloved of great poets. Its name is given after the earth.” – Classical literature

Example Shloka: हरिणी सप्तदशाक्षरा छन्दो लघुगुरुसमन्विता। मृगाणां गतिसादृश्यात्तस्याः हरिणिका कथा॥
Transliteration: hariṇī saptadaśākṣarā chando laghuguru samanvitā | mṛgāṇāṃ gatisādṛśyāt tasyāḥ hariṇikā kathā ||
Translation/Source: “Harini has seventeen syllables, endowed with short and long syllables. Due to its resemblance to the gait of deer, it is called Harini.” – Prosody texts

Example Shloka: चम्पकमाला पञ्चदशाक्षरा सुन्दरा गुरुलघुमिश्रा। पुष्पमालेव शोभते काव्ये मधुरगन्धसहिता॥
Transliteration: champakamālā pañcadaśākṣarā sundarā gurulghmiśrā | puṣpamāleva śobhate kāvye madhuragandhhasahitā ||
Translation/Source: “Champakamala has fifteen syllables, beautiful, mixed with heavy and light. Like a flower garland, it adorns poetry with sweet fragrance.” – Classical poetry

Example Shloka: कुसुमितलतावेल्लता नवदशाक्षरसमन्विता महती। पुष्पलतामिव विकसिता काव्यवनमण्डने शोभते सुन्दरी॥
Transliteration: kusumitalatāvellatā navadaśākṣarasamanvitā mahatī | puṣpalatāmiva vikasitā kāvyavanamaṇḍane śobhate sundarī ||
Translation/Source: “Kusumitalatavellatā, having nineteen syllables, is great. Like a flowering creeper in bloom, the beautiful one adorns the forest of poetry.” – Ornate literature

Example Shloka: औपच्छन्दसिकं छन्दो वैदिकं बहुरूपकम्। उपच्छन्दसि संस्थाने विविधं तत्प्रकीर्तितम्॥
Transliteration: aupacchandasikaṃ chando vaidikaṃ bahurūpakam | upacchandasi saṃsthāne vividhaṃ tat prakīrtitam ||
Translation/Source: “Aupacchandasika meter is Vedic and multiform. It is declared to be varied in its sub-metrical arrangement.” – Vedic prosody

Example Shloka: गीतिः संगीतसंस्था स्यान्मात्राकालप्रधाना सा। तालबद्धा मधुरा च गानसंस्कारशोभिता॥
Transliteration: gītiḥ saṃgītasaṃsthā syān mātrākālapradhānā sā | tālabaddhā madhurā ca gānasaṃskāraśobhitā ||
Translation/Source: “Giti is a musical arrangement, primarily based on matra-time. It is bound by rhythm, sweet, and adorned with musical refinement.” – Music treatises

Example Shloka: उद्गीतिरुच्चैर्गानस्था उत्कर्षविधिसाधना। मात्राकालनिबद्धा च गीतिकाव्ययोजना॥
Transliteration: udgītir uccair gānasthā utkarṣavidhisādhanā | mātrākālanibaddhā ca gītikāvyayojanā ||
Translation/Source: “Udgiti is established in high song, achieving excellence in method. It is bound by matra-time and employed in lyrical poetry.” – Classical treatises
